findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "authorize_certified_letter" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prepare_certified_letter, check_certified_letter, search, fetch, connect_my_letters, list_my_letters, get_my_letter · Private data: prepare_certified_letter, get_certified_letter_status, check_certified_letter, check_notice_requirement, authorize_certified_letter, get_my_letter · Public sink: prepare_certified_letter, quote_certified_letter, check_certified_letter, compare_certified_mail_services, check_notice_requirement, connect_my_letters.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prepare_certified_letter, check_certified_letter, search, fetch, connect_my_letters, list_my_letters, get_my_letter · Private data: prepare_certified_letter, get_certified_letter_status, check_certified_letter, check_notice_requirement, authorize_certified_letter, get_my_letter · Public sink: prepare_certified_letter, quote_certified_letter, check_certified_letter, compare_certified_mail_services, check_notice_requirement, connect_my_letters

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
